mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3% (as observed at t-1mo) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuation multiples, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 3%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-positive).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.5% (as observed in the latest CPIAUCSL data) signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to delay rate cuts and compressing equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL MoM change exceeds 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate below 4% (UNRATE) and rise in industrial production above 115 (INDPRO) signals an overheating economy, prompting the Federal Reserve to delay rate cuts and compress equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4% AND INDPRO > 115, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined as FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes compress equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, increasing wage pressures and inflation expectations, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 2000 thousand units (HOUST) signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 2000, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% (FEDFUNDS) within the last month signals an immediate tightening of monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts below 2000 (HOUST) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 350000 million dollars signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 2000 AND RSAFS < 350000, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p<0.05 for the one-sided test that the mean return is non-negative).
